statutory_powers: Securities Contracts (Regulation) Act, 1956 and SEBI Act, 1992
applies_to: Recognised stock exchanges and recognised clearing corporations
Anyone acquiring or holding shares in an exchange or clearing corporation, including banks, insurers and other financial institutions
key_concepts: Recognition, ownership and governance of stock exchanges and clearing corporations
Ownership limits: at least 51% public holding in a recognised stock exchange (reg 17(1))
Fit and proper test for every shareholder of an exchange or clearing corporation (reg 19)
An exchange may not list securities of its own associates (reg 45(2))
core_obligations: reg 17(2): no person resident in India may hold more than 5% of a recognised stock exchange's paid-up equity, alone or with persons acting in concert; a stock exchange, depository, banking company, insurance company or public financial institution may hold up to 15%

reg 17(3) and (4): a person resident outside India may hold up to 5% (up to 15% for a foreign exchange, depository, bank, insurer, commodity derivatives exchange or approved multilateral institution), and combined foreign holding is capped at 49%

reg 18: at least 51% of a recognised clearing corporation must be held by recognised stock exchanges; other Indian residents may hold up to 5% (15% for a depository, bank, insurer or public financial institution)
reg 19(1): no person may acquire or hold equity shares or voting rights in an exchange or clearing corporation unless fit and proper; the exchange or clearing corporation must ensure this
reg 17(5): a clearing corporation may not hold any stake in a recognised stock exchange

key_concepts: Two-stage process on NSE's NEAPS portal: in-principle approval before the issue, then a final listing application after allotment

First-time issuers also file incorporation papers, MoA and AoA, three years' annual reports and, for an NBFC, RBI's certificate showing whether it is deposit-taking or not
The GID must carry audited or limited-review financials not older than six months, audited by a peer-reviewed auditor

Final listing documents: depository credit confirmation; board or committee resolutions authorising the borrowing and the allotment with the list of allottees; debenture trust deed; GID and KID; rating; DT due diligence certificate; LPCC confirmation of the settlement guarantee fund contribution; material contracts; REF (where NSE is the designated exchange); listing fees; SEBI fee of Rs 5,000 per KID
core_obligations: Obtain NSE's in-principle approval before giving the placement memorandum and term sheet (GID and KID) to the EBP, or before the issue opens where EBP does not apply

Pay fees into the issuer's PAN-based virtual account at IDBI Bank

key_concepts: Covers deals, collateral, margins, clearing and settlement, the core settlement guarantee fund, charges and penalties, tri-party (basket) repo and negotiated trades reported on the BSE-ICDM portal
Earlier notices on the subject stand rescinded; where a notice conflicts with the master circular, the notice prevails
core_obligations: Follow the master circular for clearing and settlement of debt trades through ICCL
instruments.consequences_general: Securities Contracts (Regulation) Act, 1956: a listed entity must comply with the conditions of its listing agreement (s. 21); a recognised stock exchange may delist securities on the prescribed grounds after recording reasons (s. 21A); failure to comply with listing or delisting conditions attracts a penalty of Rs 5 lakh to Rs 25 crore (s. 23E), and breach of the Act, rules, the exchange's bye-laws or regulations or SEBI directions with no separate penalty attracts a penalty under s. 23H. instruments.short_name: Liquidity Window Facility for bond investors
instruments.title: Revised operating guidelines for the Liquidity Window Facility for investors in debt securities, with issuer compliance requirements
instruments.issuing_department: National Stock Exchange of India Ltd
instruments.theme: Bond trading, settlement and liquidity
instruments.reference_no: NSE/DS/72742 (11-02-2026) and NSE/CML/2026/1 (04-05-2026), under SEBI circular SEBI/HO/DDHS/DDHS-PoD-1/P/CIR/2024/141 of 16-10-2024
applies_to: Issuers that offer investors a put option through the exchange's liquidity window
Investors in those debt securities, through brokers or OBPPs
key_concepts: Investors exercise the put through the exchange during the window; securities are blocked in their demat accounts by early pay-in
Eligible investors are fixed on T-2 (T is the first day of the window); allocation is in full or proportionate, all categories at par; a retail-only window is capped at Rs 2 lakh per investor
core_obligations: Disclose the exchanges, eligible investor categories and method in the offer document
Give notice of each window on NEAPS at least 3 working days before it opens, and apply with the list of eligible investors, a confirmation and a board resolution at least 2 working days before
Upload the put price from a SEBI-registered rating agency's valuation by 6 p.m. on T-1
Appoint an RTA for allocation and a clearing member for settlement; name a designated exchange if more than one is used
timelines: Window open 9 a.m. to 5 p.m.; bids to the RTA on T+2; allocation file to the clearing corporations by 12.30 p.m. on T+3; settlement on T+4 on a gross basis without settlement guarantee
Post-window disclosures within three working days
consequences_stated: If the issuer's clearing member does not fund in full, investors are not paid and their securities are returned
